sourceTraceSupplement.text: Keyboard focus must remain visible. When removing a queue occurrence whose Remove button owns focus, move to the next visible Remove action, then the previous visible one, or Close queue if none remain. Skip collapsed Earlier history and reveal only the needed distance above the player; removing a repeated song must remove only that occurrence. Leave focus elsewhere untouched. In All songs, albums and playlists, keep the focused song row and its checkbox, artwork, title and actions clear of the sticky heading, selection toolbar, player and changing playback notices. Arrow navigation follows each key press, including quick repeats. Reveal only the needed distance; pointer selection and passive updates must not scroll the list or take focus from a dialog or menu. Keyboard focus must leave filter popups and song action menus naturally with Tab, return after dialogs, and return to the relevant setup control after managing sources, DJs, or provider keys without losing the draft. Opening a playlist name, source name, or new listening-room name form puts focus in its name field so typing works immediately. The Add to playlist form initially focuses the new-playlist name, and choosing Create a new playlist again focuses its newly shown name field. Editing values, changing source type, or background refreshes must not move focus back. Help and confirmation dialogs start on a safe non-destructive target. Escape, Cancel, Close and backdrop dismissal return focus to the opening control when it remains available. If a dialog removes its opening control, focus the current page heading. Keep long dialog titles compact so Close and keyboard actions remain reachable at the current acceptance baseline. Preserve the full accessible title. For DJ and source deletion, show the complete target name in wrapping body text so similarly named items remain distinguishable before confirmation. Give related source checkboxes a group name and keep interactive recovery controls outside live status/error announcements.
